title: Hosted vs Dedicated: Residency tradeoffs & rollout brainstorm
content:
Purpose:
This is a working brainstorm comparing Hosted vs Dedicated approaches for satisfying customer data residency requirements. Aim: surface concrete enforcement options, telemetry and validation approaches, rollout shape for customers who need region pinning, and the practical tradeoffs for ops and sales.

Background / context:
- We have multiple asks from enterprise accounts: full in-region data processing, log residency, and strict cloud provider constraints.
- Hosted API provides easy UX but complicates strict legal/data-residency commitments. Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) gives stronger guarantees but higher ops and cost.
- This doc assumes the core runtime supports runtime-routing, region tags on requests, model-variant pinning, and KV/cache scoping by region. It also assumes we have a basic per-customer metadata store with fields like "preferred_region", "residency_level".

Assumptions:
- "Region" refers to cloud region + tenancy (e.g., aws-eu-west-1-hosted, azure-eu-north-dedicated).
- Customers can request: ANY, REGION_PREFERRED, REGION_PINNED, or PRIVATE_ONPREM.
- We do not attempt legal advice here — this is engineering/ops planning.

High-level tradeoffs (notes / discussion items):
- Compliance guarantee:
  - Hosted: soft guarantees (best-effort routing, copy-locational restrictions for persisted data) but logs/telemetry may cross borders unless we add strict controls.
  - Dedicated: stronger SLA-level guarantees; full isolation possible.
- Cost & Velocity:
  - Hosted: low onboarding friction, multi-tenant efficiencies, faster feature shipping.
  - Dedicated: higher onboarding time for reservations, more expensive per token but easier to meet strict residency.
- Operational complexity:
  - Hosted: simpler infra but requires robust region routing and audit controls to avoid accidental cross-region writes.
  - Dedicated: requires provisioning pipelines, capacity planning, peri-customer autoscaling, and lifecycle management.
- Failure modes and fallback:
  - Hosted: automatic fallback to nearest region might violate residency. Need customer-configurable fallback policies (allow/deny).
  - Dedicated: in-outage fallback to hosted must be explicit and customer opt-in.

Enforcement options we could implement (ranked rough by effort):
1) Soft-tag routing + telemetry (low effort): attach region_hint to request, prefer same-region pools, log when served outside region. No hard-blocks.
2) Hard pin at gateway (medium effort): gateway enforces customer's residency_level; returns 409/422 if unavailable. Provide admin override for sales/ops.
3) Policy engine with exception rules (medium-high effort): per-tenant policies, time-bound exceptions, audit trail, Jira-backed approval flows.
4) Dedicated reservations (high effort): customers provision dedicated clusters in target region; enforcement is structural.
5) On-prem package (very high effort): customer self-host or air-gapped; Redwood provides private control-plane connectors.

Suggested telemetry & validation plan (what we measure and how):
- Per-request tags: request_region_hint, actual_execution_region, storage_region, log_ingest_region (all persisted to telemetry).
- Periodic residency audit: nightly job that queries recent requests for any region mismatches for REGION_PINNED tenants. Generates report + alerts.
- Continuous sampling: for soft-mode customers sample 1% of traffic and validate path end-to-end.
- SLA dashboards: percent of requests served in-region, broken down by tenant and model.

Example enforcement policy pseudocode (gateway-level):
- tenant.residency_level == "REGION_PINNED" -> require actual_execution_region == tenant.preferred_region OR reject request
- tenant.residency_level == "REGION_PREFERRED" -> prefer preferred_region, but allowed fallback with telemetry flag set
- tenant.residency_level == "ANY" -> route normally

Operational runbooks / failover patterns (sketch):
- If in-region capacity exhausted for REGION_PINNED -> automatically OPEN a ticket and notify customer; do not failover unless explicit signed exception exists.
- For REGION_PREFERRED -> fallback allowed after X seconds; log and send customer digest.
- For Dedicated clusters: automated degraded-mode notification: during network partitions, stop inbound traffic and present friendly 503 with guidance to customer portal and expected ETA.

Validation checklist for onboarding a residency customer (working list):
- Customer contract/residency SLA mapped to residency_level in metadata
- Provisioned capacity (if dedicated) in target region, smoke tests passing (latency, correct region tag on VM)
- Storage buckets created with correct region and encryption keys (KMS customer-managed if required)
- Access controls & audit logging enabled; retention policy configured per customer
- Canary traffic routed and validated for 48h; nightly residency audit shows 100% in-region for pinned customers
- Monitoring: workspace added to residency dashboard, alert thresholds set (e.g., >0.1% cross-region fails triggers paging)

Exception workflows (ideas):
- Time-limited geo-exception token (expires, auto-revoked) that can be granted by compliance team for disaster recovery
- Sales/Customer Success can request emergency fallbacks via a specific JIRA queue; action requires audit note and executive sign-off for certain classes of customers

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 - Internal validation (2 weeks): prototype gateway-enforcement in staging and run rush-hour simulation with region constraints.
Phase 1 - Early customers opt-in (4–6 weeks): invite 2-3 pilot customers with REGION_PREFERRED; collect telemetry and iterate.
Phase 2 - Beta pinned enforcement (6–10 weeks): add hard pin enforcement for a small cohort with full audit trails and runbooks.
Phase 3 - GA: support for pinned mode documented, dedicated reservation playbook published, automation for provisioning hardened.

Open questions / decision points (needs input):
- What is the default fallback policy for REGION_PREFERRED? Immediate fallback or wait N seconds? (ops + customer UX tradeoffs)
- How do we price exceptions / emergency DR fallbacks to avoid misuse?
- Which logs/telemetry are considered "restricted" and must never leave the target region? How to enforce for third party integrations?
- What is our legal posture for soft-guarantees vs contractual pinned guarantees? Need input from legal/compliance.

Notes for next meeting:
- Ask Legal for a short memo on language we can use in contracts for "best-effort" vs "pinned guarantees".
- Engineering: prototype gateway check + nightly audit job (priority P0).
- SRE: simulate capacity exhaustion scenarios and validate runbook time to recovery.
- Product/Commercial: draft pricing tiers for dedicated/residency add-on and exception fees.

Quick links / references (working):
- CONFLUENCE-2103: Residency policy primer (internal)
- JIRA-RES-78: Residency enforcement epic
- slack: #private-deployments thread "eu-cust-incident-2024"

Rough action items (owners):
- Aisha: prototype gateway-level enforcement in staging (due 2025-01-28)
- Marcus: build nightly residency audit job skeleton and sample report (due 2025-02-04)
- Eleni: coordinate legal memo request and draft contract language (due 2025-02-10)
- Priya: draft customer-facing onboarding checklist and pricing note (due 2025-02-12)

Notes to self / informal musings:
- We should avoid making "pinned" the default; sticky defaults create ops debt.
- Consider an "observability-only" mode for low-touch customers: we enforce nothing but give them a residency compliance report they can use for internal audits.
- Think about offering a time-windowed dedicated burst in region for heavy batches to reduce cost for customers who are mostly global but occasionally need in-region processing.

End of brainstorm.
